title: Arrest model: uncertainty and sensitivity analysis
context: RideBelt is an open, safety-critical Hee-Lee Oss project: an optional rider-worn backup restraint (low hip belt + short tethers; optional clip-on Shoulder Module or one-piece Integrated Harness) that latches into an open seat anchor standard (RAS). ALL safety content is DRAFT and not for use until a credentialed engineer signs off at the MVP gate (GOVERNANCE.md). Never remove a DRAFT banner, never give instructions for wearing or attaching anything to a ride, never copy text from paid standards (cite by number and title only), never name private individuals or incident victims, and respect the patent design-arounds in docs/research/patentability-fto.md. Body/belt compliance, slack, rider mass and absorber threshold are uncertain. The design load should hold across plausible ranges. Risk tier high: requires credentialed expert review before release.
objective: Add a Monte Carlo and one-at-a-time sensitivity study over k_b, slack, mass, pulse amplitude and duration, tether angle and absorber force, reporting percentiles of peak tension and excursion.
acceptanceCriteria: Parameter ranges cited or flagged ASSUMPTION
